spec_match.rationale: The codec string's four fields and the profile and substream-codec vocabulary come from the AOMedia specification, and every support answer on every page is a live call to isTypeSupported, canPlayType or decodingInfo rather than a recorded result. The ladder deliberately uses canPlayType because that is what a <source> element's type attribute is checked against, not the strictest of the three.

interactive.rationale: A nine-row three-API matrix with controls and a re-probe button; a codec-string builder whose four selects re-probe on every change and which shows one-field variations alongside; and a ladder chooser that renders the markup, highlights the rung the browser would take, and then builds a real audio element to check it.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index explains why an immersive mix is not a bigger stereo file — channel-based, scene-based and object-based presentations — and why decoding in the media pipeline removes the JavaScript decoder, which is the ChromeStatus entry's own motivation.

edge_cases.rationale: An invented codec as a negative control on every page; a wrong-cased codec token that fails identically to a wrong profile; a container that is not mp4; a ladder that could end with no playable rung; and the case where even the plain-Opus control fails, which the builder calls out as pointing at the container rather than at IAMF.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/5113656292540416 on the index and all three concept pages, with the AOMedia IAMF specification, Media Source Extensions, the HTML media load algorithm and MDN's decodingInfo.

conformance.rationale: Six immutable assertions: MSE exists; the probe itself works (a real codec yes, an invented one no); IAMF is accepted by MSE; canPlayType recognises it too; decodingInfo reports on it; and a source rejected on its type is never fetched — the last measured from resource timing, because it is the claim the ladder page rests on.

runtime_evidence.rationale: deno task drive over all three pages in real Chrome 150: 3/3, 27 assertions. Measured: 0 of 6 IAMF strings supported by any of the three APIs, while audio/mp4 Opus and AAC-LC are supported by all three in the same run and an invented codec is rejected by all three. The ladder page proved its central claim directly — the IAMF source was never requested while the two playable ones were, read from resource timing.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert with the supported counts, whether the controls behaved, the built string, and which sources were fetched.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, buttons set background and colour, 44px control minimums, and the three wide tables in their own scroll containers. Two colour assignments on the ladder page are set from JavaScript as var() references rather than classes, which is a small inconsistency worth tidying but not a raw literal.

accessibility.rationale: The matrix and variation tables are semantic with row headers; every verdict is a sentence carrying the measured values; the ladder marks each rung's state in text as well as by border; results are announced through aria-live; the generated audio element is a real one with controls.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Control grids are auto-fit minmax and stack at 360px; the ladder rows use a three-column grid whose middle column wraps; every table and the markup block scroll inside their own containers.

openQuestions.title: Ship a real IAMF file to play once a browser can decode it
openQuestions.detail: The ladder's sources are URLs that deliberately 404, which is enough to prove what was fetched and not enough to prove anything plays. A short IAMF asset alongside a stereo fallback would turn the last page from a demonstration of source selection into a demonstration of immersive audio — and would need a decision about hosting a media file in this repository, which nothing here currently does.

openQuestions.title: Nothing here exercises the three presentation types
openQuestions.detail: The index explains that IAMF carries channel-based, scene-based and object-based audio, and no page demonstrates the difference — because without a decoder there is nothing to render and without an asset there is nothing to decode. A page that visualises a mix presentation, or that rotates an ambisonic field against head position, is the obvious next concept and needs both.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive support matrix table without horizontal page overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Wide tabular content belongs in its own scroll container; control panels should auto-fit and stack.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The nine-row matrix, the field table and the variation table each sit in an overflow-x:auto wrapper because their columns are nowrap by design — codec strings must not wrap mid-token — and the builder's four selects are an auto-fit grid.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: responsive-check desktop + mobile on the feature.

guidanceConsulted.query: announce asynchronous probe results in a live region
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Results that arrive after a promise resolves must be announced, and a control that starts them should disable while they run.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Every page writes its conclusion into an aria-live output once all three APIs have answered; the matrix's re-probe button disables during the run; each verdict names the measured values rather than relying on a colour.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive waits on the announced text on each page before asserting.

guidanceConsulted.query: source element type attribute and media load algorithm
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Give every <source> a type attribute so the element can reject it without a request, and order sources by preference.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: This is the feature under demonstration on the third page, and the claim is proved rather than repeated: resource timing shows the IAMF source was never requested while the two playable ones were.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Measured: fetched 2 of 3 sources; the rung above the chosen one was never requested.

summary: Three concepts about a format this browser cannot decode, built so that every negative is trustworthy: controls on every page, three APIs asked the same question, and a source ladder whose central claim — a type attribute saves the download — is proved from resource timing. Building it corrected one page: currentSrc reports the last source an element tried, not the first one it accepted, so a ladder whose files 404 makes it a misleading signal.
